blonde-redhead>sonic-youth.note: Two searches. The only lead is a Pitchfork conversation with Kazu Makino (her influential albums), which I never reached. A FarOut Magazine article paraphrasing it has her saying Sonic Youth, Beck and Nirvana were 'bands I loved but definitely didn't identify with', so that page may not support SY as an influence. Another page I found, a BmoreArt interview (bmoreart.com/2024/04/standing-firm-at-thirty-an-interview-with-blonde-redheads-kazu-makino.html), only has the interviewer saying the band was compared to Sonic Youth. To check: open the Pitchfork page and look for a first-person Sonic Youth line; if there is none, mark it 'decide' (comparison only).

blonde-redhead>my-bloody-valentine.note: Two searches. The Pitchfork Kazu Makino page never surfaced. FarOut Magazine says Makino told Pitchfork about hitting a 'wall of noise sound' during her early New York years: 'It was Lush and My Bloody Valentine.' That is probably the right first-person influence source, but I haven't opened the original. A TIDAL Magazine interview (tidal.com/magazine/article/blonde-redhead-its-almost-too-personal/1-8869) has her saying 'And of course My Bloody Valentine – they're so soothing', but that is an admired-sound answer, not influence. To check: open the Pitchfork page and copy the exact sentence.

broken-social-scene>talk-talk.note: The SPIN 'My Favorite Things' page (May 2011) carries the quoted text, with Kevin Drew naming 'Laughing Stock by Talk Talk' under FAVORITE ALBUM. It is a favourite-album answer about authentic emotion, with no statement that Talk Talk shaped Drew's or Broken Social Scene's own music. Per the rules that is a favourites-list-type answer, not influence. Proposal: remove, or keep only if a better source turns up. A lead is Drew's Brooklyn Vegan '10 favorite ballads' list (New Grass by Talk Talk), which I did not open.

broken-social-scene>dirty-three.note: Same SPIN 'My Favorite Things' page: Drew's FAVORITE ALBUM answer names 'Whatever You Love, You Are by the Dirty Three' as among the most authentic human emotion on an album. It is a present-tense favourite with no claim of influence on his own music. Proposal: remove, or keep only if a better source turns up. A separate Arcana interview of Drew has him listing Dirty Three among his 'favourite bands', which is also not an influence statement.

mudhoney>wipers.note: One search. The Life of the Record (Talkhouse) podcast page (talkhouse.com/the-making-of-superfuzz-bigmuff-by-mudhoney-featuring-mark-arm-and-steve-turner) is a summary with no transcript, and the quote would be in the audio. Lead: Rolling Stone Italia, 'Senza i Wipers non ci sarebbero stati i Nirvana' (rollingstone.it/?p=529722), reports in Italian that Steve Turner called 'No One Has' the 'Wipers song' and that Turner and Arm formed Green River partly inspired by the Wipers. That would be tier 'reported', and I haven't opened it. Better to find the English original of that piece, or a transcript of the podcast.

perfume-genius>xiu-xiu.note: The Fader podcast write-up (9 August 2021) carries the quoted words: Hadreas says 'there's some music like Xiu Xiu, who I love, where their songs are so intense and visceral and over the top...' He is using Xiu Xiu as an example of how his reaction to one intense song changes from day to day (devastating one day, campy the next). It is a present-tense fan remark in an aside about listening, not a statement that Xiu Xiu shaped his own music, so it falls under 'what I'm listening to now'. Proposal: remove, or keep only if a better source turns up. I read it from the search tool's page extract, not through a separate fetch.

squid>tortoise.note: The Amherst Student interview (23 February 2021) has Borlase naming Tortoise's Millions Now Living Will Never Die first in his 'five albums for the rest of your life' list: 'They have this cool electronic sound, without vocals, and it kind of challenged a lot of the boundaries that they had at the time.' That is a favourites-list answer with praise, but he does not say Tortoise shaped Squid or his own playing; he does say 'It really influenced my taste' about the Philip Glass entry in the same list. Proposal: remove, or keep only as a weak link and look for a statement of influence. It is not a Loud And Quiet piece as the citation says.
